natural: jump down a well to save someone

meaning.en: To rescue someone in a way that gets oneself into the same danger; a well-meant but foolish sacrifice.
meaning.zh: 跳进井里去救人，比喻冒险救人而害了自己，也指不顾自身安危的无益牺牲。

equivalents: a rescue that only adds a victim
jump in after someone and drown too

examples.zh: 不会水就跳下去，那是从井救人，没用的。
examples.en: Jumping in when you can't swim is a rescue that only adds a victim.

examples.zh: 帮朋友也要量力，不能从井救人。
examples.en: Help your friend within your means; don't throw yourself in after him.

story.en: Zai Wo asks Confucius whether a humane man, told that someone has fallen into a well, would jump in after him; Confucius says he would go and see, but not be trapped.
story.zh: 《论语·雍也》：“宰我问曰：‘仁者，虽告之曰，井有仁焉，其从之也？’子曰：‘何为其然也？君子可逝也，不可陷也。’”

usage.en: Usually a warning against reckless self-sacrifice; the original text uses it to question a naive case of ‘benevolence’.
usage.zh: 多用于劝诫不要盲目冒险；原文借以反问仁者是否会这样做。

natural: coarse clothes and untidy hair

meaning.en: Plain clothes and untidy hair, yet natural beauty still shows through.
meaning.zh: 衣着粗朴，头发凌乱，形容不加修饰；也指虽不修饰仍显天然美。

examples.zh: 她粗服乱头，却依然光彩照人。
examples.en: In rough clothes and untidy hair, she still shone.

examples.zh: 画中的渔家女粗服乱头，却质朴动人。
examples.en: The fisher girl in the painting has coarse clothes and tousled hair, yet is simple and touching.

usage.en: May be mild criticism of untidiness or praise of unaffected beauty; compare 不修边幅.
usage.zh: 可批评不修边幅，也可赞天然之美；可参看“不修边幅”。

natural: advance an inch, retreat a foot

meaning.en: Little gain and great loss; progress that is outweighed by setbacks.
meaning.zh: 前进一寸，后退一尺，比喻进步少而损失多。

equivalents: one step forward, many steps back

examples.zh: 项目寸进尺退，进展始终有限。
examples.en: The project gains an inch and loses a foot, and progress remains small.

examples.zh: 谈判寸进尺退，双方互不让步。
examples.en: The negotiation gave a little and lost a lot, with neither side yielding.

story.en: Laozi quotes a military saying: 'I dare not take the lead but prefer to be guest; I dare not advance an inch but retreat a foot.'
story.zh: 《老子》第六十九章：“吾不敢为主而为客，不敢进寸而退尺。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前6—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 6th–4th c. BC

usage.en: Opposite in grammar to 得寸进尺 (greedy); reads 寸 cùn, 尺 chǐ. Describes slow or setback-ridden progress.
usage.zh: 与“得寸进尺”不同；描述进展缓慢、反复受挫。

natural: an inch of shadow, a foot of jade

meaning.en: Time is more precious than a great jade disc; a reminder to value every moment.
meaning.zh: 一寸光阴比一尺的璧玉还珍贵，比喻时间极其宝贵。

equivalents: time is worth more than jade

examples.zh: 寸阴尺璧，同学们要珍惜青春。
examples.en: Time is worth more than jade; students, treasure your youth.

examples.zh: 他把寸阴尺璧的道理牢记在心。
examples.en: He kept in mind that time is more precious than treasure.

story.en: Huainanzi says the sage does not prize a foot of jade but values an inch of shadow, since time is hard to meet and easy to lose.
story.zh: 《淮南子·原道训》：“圣人不贵尺之璧，而重寸之阴，时难得而易失也。”

usage.en: Exhortation to value time; 寸阴 means a very short span of time, measured by the inch a sundial shadow moves.
usage.zh: 劝人珍惜时间；“寸阴”指极短的时间，原指日影移动一寸。

natural: handle with ease and to spare

meaning.en: To handle matters calmly and comfortably, with plenty of ability in reserve.
meaning.zh: 处理事情从容不迫，游刃有余。

examples.zh: 面对突发状况，他措置裕如。
examples.en: Faced with the emergency, he handled things with ease.

examples.zh: 这位老教师处理课堂纠纷措置裕如。
examples.en: The veteran teacher handled classroom disputes with calm ease.

usage.en: Praises composure and competence; 措置 means 'to manage'. Formal.
usage.zh: 称赞从容有能力；“措置”即处理；较正式。

natural: inlaid colours and carved gold

meaning.en: Highly ornate, finely wrought style in art or literature; may suggest over-decoration.
meaning.zh: 色彩交错，金饰雕镂，形容诗文或工艺华丽精美，也含过分雕琢之意。

examples.zh: 这首长诗错彩镂金，辞藻极尽华美。
examples.en: This long poem is richly ornate and dazzlingly worded.

examples.zh: 宫殿内错彩镂金，令人眼花缭乱。
examples.en: Inside the palace everything is inlaid and gilded, dazzling to the eye.

story.en: Critic Bao Zhao compared the poetry of Xie Lingyun to a lotus emerging from water, natural and lovely, and that of Yan Yanzhi to inlaid colours and carved gold.
story.zh: 《南史·颜延之传》载鲍照语：“谢五言如初发芙蓉，自然可爱；君诗若铺锦列绣，亦雕缋满眼。”，后世以“错彩镂金”概括颜诗的雕琢华丽

usage.en: Often set against 芙蓉出水 (natural beauty) in criticism; a contrast of ornate and plain styles.
usage.zh: 评论中常与“芙蓉出水”（自然清新）对照。

natural: raise one's spirit, stamp with vigour

meaning.en: Vigorous, spirited and full of determination.
meaning.zh: 精神奋发，意气昂扬，行动勇猛。

examples.zh: 队员们发扬蹈厉，士气高昂。
examples.en: The team members were full of spirit and morale was high.

examples.zh: 新一代科研人员发扬蹈厉，勇攀高峰。
examples.en: The new generation of researchers is full of drive and aims for the summit.

story.en: The Book of Rites describes the dance for King Wu's victory, in which the dancers' stamping and lifting movements show the king's vigorous conquering spirit.
story.zh: 《礼记·乐记》：“发扬蹈厉，太公之志也。”

usage.en: Praise for energetic spirit. Do not confuse 发扬 with 发扬光大 (carry forward); 厉 means fierce.
usage.zh: 赞扬精神昂扬；注意与“发扬光大”不同，“厉”指猛烈。

natural: expose wickedness and unearth hidden deeds

meaning.en: To bring hidden crimes and secret wrongdoers to light; of a sharp, incisive official.
meaning.zh: 揭发奸邪，查出隐藏的坏人坏事，多形容官吏明察秋毫。

examples.zh: 这位法官发奸擿伏，不放过任何疑点。
examples.en: This judge exposes hidden wrongs and lets no doubtful point pass.

examples.zh: 纪检部门发奸擿伏，查出多起贪腐案件。
examples.en: The disciplinary body ferreted out concealed corruption and uncovered several cases.

story.en: The Han Shu praises Zhao Guanghan, governor of the capital, who was skilled at ferreting out hidden crimes (‘钩距’) and exposing evil.
story.zh: 《汉书·赵广汉传》称其“发奸擿伏如神”。

usage.en: Praise for sharp investigators; 擿 is read tī here (to dig up).
usage.zh: 赞扬明察的官吏；“擿”读 tī，挑出之意。

natural: no way to split oneself

meaning.en: To be so busy that one cannot be in two places at once; unable to attend to everything.
meaning.zh: 忙得不能同时顾及几件事，没有分身的办法。

equivalents: can't be in two places at once

examples.zh: 两个会议同时开，我分身乏术。
examples.en: Two meetings are on at the same time and I can't be in two places.

examples.zh: 她又要工作又要带孩子，常常分身乏术。
examples.en: Between work and the kids she is often stretched thin.

usage.en: A common polite excuse for being unable to attend or help; 分身无术 is an equally common written form.
usage.zh: 常作无法分身赴约或协助时的委婉说法；“分身无术”也常见。

natural: the phoenix sings toward the morning sun

meaning.en: A sign of a fine age: rare talent appears in an era of good rule.
meaning.zh: 凤凰在朝阳下鸣叫，比喻贤才遇到好时机，也象征天下太平的吉兆。

equivalents: a sign of an age of excellence
talent flourishing in a good era

examples.zh: 盛世之下，贤才辈出，正如凤鸣朝阳。
examples.en: In a flourishing age talents emerge in numbers, like the phoenix crying to the dawn.

examples.zh: 这篇贺词用凤鸣朝阳祝愿新秀前程似锦。
examples.en: The greeting uses the phoenix and the morning sun to wish the newcomer a bright future.

story.en: The ode 'Juan'e' says: 'The phoenix cries on that high hill; the wutong grows on that sunlit slope.'
story.zh: 《诗经·大雅·卷阿》：“凤凰鸣矣，于彼高冈；梧桐生矣，于彼朝阳。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Auspicious image; 朝 reads zhāo ('morning'). Used in congratulations or praise of an era.
usage.zh: 吉祥意象；“朝”读 zhāo（早晨）；用于祝贺或赞美时代。

natural: prop up the perilous, steady the tottering

meaning.en: To rescue a state or situation from danger and restore stability.
meaning.zh: 扶助危难，稳定倾覆的局面。

examples.zh: 总理在金融危机中扶危定倾，稳住了大局。
examples.en: In the financial crisis the premier steadied the whole situation.

examples.zh: 他临危受命，扶危定倾，挽救了公司。
examples.en: Taking charge in a crisis, he rescued the company and restored stability.

usage.en: Praise for heroic leaders in a crisis; formal.
usage.zh: 赞扬危难中力挽狂澜的人；较正式。

natural: a drifting soul in the bottom of a cauldron

meaning.en: A person or force that is doomed and will not survive long.
meaning.zh: 锅底游动的魂魄，比喻处境危险、即将灭亡的人或势力。

examples.zh: 那股残余势力已成釜底游魂，难成气候。
examples.en: The remnants are now doomed and cannot make any headway.

examples.zh: 他自知是釜底游魂，却还想负隅顽抗。
examples.en: He knew he was done for, yet still hoped to make a last stand.

usage.en: Contemptuous, used in political or military contexts of an enemy near its end.
usage.zh: 带轻蔑，多用于政治、军事上走投无路的对手。

natural: a general who is shield and wall

meaning.en: A brave general who defends the country like a shield and a city wall.
meaning.zh: 像盾牌和城墙一样捍卫国家的将领。

examples.zh: 他是国家的干城之将，守住了边疆。
examples.en: He is a general of the nation's defence, who held the frontier.

examples.zh: 军中需要更多干城之将。
examples.en: The army needs more stalwart commanders like walls and shields.

story.en: In 'Tu Ju', the lord's stalwart warriors are praised as 'shield and wall' of the marquis and duke.
story.zh: 《诗经·周南·兔罝》：“赳赳武夫，公侯干城。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Praise for loyal, capable military leaders; 干 means 'shield' (gān), not 'dry'.
usage.zh: 赞扬忠勇有才的将领；“干”指盾牌，读 gān。

natural: a lofty mountain and a great road

meaning.en: Noble virtue that one looks up to and follows; a model of moral excellence.
meaning.zh: 崇高的德行，让人仰慕和效法。

examples.zh: 孔子是后世仰慕的高山景行。
examples.en: Confucius is the lofty example to whom later generations look up.

examples.zh: 他高山景行的品格，影响了几代学生。
examples.en: His noble character has influenced several generations of students.

story.en: The ode 'Chexia' says: 'Looking up to the high mountain, one follows the great road.'
story.zh: 《诗经·小雅·车舝》：“高山仰止，景行行止。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Often used with 高山仰止: admiration for great figures. Read 行 as xíng.
usage.zh: 常与“高山仰止”连用，表示敬仰大德之人；“行”读 xíng。

natural: not even as good as a dog or a pig

meaning.en: Contemptible and worse than an animal; a strong condemnation of base conduct.
meaning.zh: 连猪狗都不如，形容品行卑劣到极点。

examples.zh: 他抛弃年迈的父母，真是狗彘不如。
examples.en: He abandoned his aged parents; he is lower than a beast.

examples.zh: 这种欺压孤儿的行径简直狗彘不如。
examples.en: Bullying orphans like this is simply worse than animal behaviour.

usage.en: A harsh insult; use only in strong moral condemnation. 彘 reads zhì.
usage.zh: 严厉斥责，仅用于强烈道德谴责；“彘”读 zhì。

natural: caps and carriage-canopies in each other's sight

meaning.en: A stream of officials or envoys travelling, so that one's carriage can be seen right after another's.
meaning.zh: 使者、官员的车辆络绎不绝，前后相望。

examples.zh: 两国交往密切，使者冠盖相望。
examples.en: The two states had close relations and envoys travelled in a constant stream.

examples.zh: 峰会期间各国代表冠盖相望，热闹非凡。
examples.en: During the summit delegates came in a procession, making it very lively.

usage.en: Describes busy diplomatic or official traffic; 冠 here is guān, 盖 is gài.
usage.zh: 形容使节或官员往来频繁；“冠”读 guān，“盖”读 gài。

natural: Guan Fu cursing the company

meaning.en: To lose one's temper and abuse guests at a banquet, venting one's grievances in public.
meaning.zh: 西汉灌夫在酒席上辱骂宾客，比喻借酒发泄不满、当众骂人。

equivalents: vent one's temper at a feast

examples.zh: 他喝醉后灌夫骂座，弄得宴会不欢而散。
examples.en: He got drunk and abused the guests, and the party broke up on a sour note.

examples.zh: 别学灌夫骂座，有话好好说。
examples.en: Don't rant at the table like Guan Fu; say what you have to say calmly.

story.en: At a banquet, Guan Fu, drunk, cursed the guests and Prime Minister Tian Fen, which led to the downfall of Guan Fu and the Marquis of Weiqi.
story.zh: 《史记·魏其武安侯列传》载灌夫在田蚡婚宴上使酒骂座，遂被劾下狱。

usage.en: Allusion to a historical figure; can describe a rude outburst or admire a blunt, brave protest, depending on tone.
usage.zh: 典故；视语气可指无礼发作，也可指直言抗争。

natural: prize the ear, scorn the eye

meaning.en: To believe what one hears and ignore what one sees; to trust hearsay over firsthand evidence.
meaning.zh: 相信传闻而轻视亲眼所见，指不重事实、盲信传言。

examples.zh: 别贵耳贱目，亲自去调查才有发言权。
examples.en: Don't trust hearsay over evidence; you can only speak after investigating yourself.

examples.zh: 他贵耳贱目，被谣言牵着走。
examples.en: He believes hearsay and ignores what he sees, and is led around by rumours.

story.en: Zhang Heng's 'Eastern Capital Rhapsody' mocks shallow scholars who 'value the ear and despise the eye'.
story.zh: 张衡《东京赋》：“若客所谓，末学肤受，贵耳而贱目者也。”

usage.en: Warns against uncritical belief in rumours; often paired with 贵远贱近 in older writing.
usage.zh: 劝诫不要盲信传言；旧文中常与“贵远贱近”并说。

natural: speak beyond the facts

meaning.en: To exaggerate; to put matters more strongly than the facts warrant.
meaning.zh: 把话说得过分，言过其实。

examples.zh: 广告说得过甚其词，实际效果并不明显。
examples.en: The advertisement overstates its case and the actual effect is small.

examples.zh: 他谈到困难时有些过甚其词。
examples.en: He was a bit exaggerated when he spoke of the difficulties.

usage.en: A formal way of saying 'exaggerate'; 其词 means 'one's words'. Usually a criticism.
usage.zh: “夸大其词”的书面说法，“其词”指他的话；一般带批评意味。

natural: the autumn cicadas' piteous cry

meaning.en: The mournful sound of cicadas in late autumn, evoking parting and sadness.
meaning.zh: 深秋蝉声凄凉悲切，常渲染离别或伤感的气氛。

examples.zh: 傍晚的郊外，寒蝉凄切，令人黯然神伤。
examples.en: In the evening countryside the cicadas cry mournfully and dishearten the traveller.

examples.zh: 车站送别时，寒蝉凄切，更添愁绪。
examples.en: As they said farewell at the station, the mournful cicadas deepened the sorrow.

story.en: Liu Yong's farewell lyric opens: 'The cold cicadas cry mournfully; at the evening pavilion the shower has just ceased.'
story.zh: 柳永《雨霖铃》：“寒蝉凄切，对长亭晚，骤雨初歇。”

usage.en: Poetic scene-setting for parting; 切 reads qiè as 'sharp, piercing'. Note 凄切 is qī qiè.
usage.zh: 诗意的场景铺垫，多渲染离愁；“切”在此读 qiè。

natural: great houses and noble heirs

meaning.en: Powerful families and the children of nobles; the upper class.
meaning.zh: 有权势的家族和显贵的后代，泛指上层社会。

examples.zh: 她出身豪门贵胄，却过着朴素的生活。
examples.en: She comes from a great family, yet lives simply.

examples.zh: 小说描写了豪门贵胄的恩怨纠葛。
examples.en: The novel depicts the feuds and entanglements of noble families.

usage.en: Neutral to mildly critical of privilege; 胄 reads zhòu (descendants).
usage.zh: 中性或略含对特权的批评；“胄”读 zhòu，后裔之意。

natural: a snowflake on a great furnace

meaning.en: Instantly resolved, like a snowflake melting on a blazing furnace; doubts or troubles vanish at once.
meaning.zh: 一点雪落在大炉上立即融化，比喻疑虑、烦恼等一下子消失；也指在大才面前微不足道。

equivalents: melt away like snow in a furnace

examples.zh: 听了老师的讲解，心中疑惑洪炉点雪般消散。
examples.en: After the teacher's explanation, my doubts melted away like snow in a furnace.

examples.zh: 再大的烦恼，到了她面前也洪炉点雪。
examples.en: However great my worries, they vanish before her.

usage.en: Of sudden enlightenment or the easy dissolving of trouble; often Chan (Zen) in flavour.
usage.zh: 指豁然开悟或烦恼轻易消散；带禅宗意味。

natural: sun and moon inside a pot

meaning.en: A separate, carefree world; the leisure and detachment of a recluse or immortal.
meaning.zh: 壶中另有天地，比喻仙境或隐逸者悠闲自在的生活。

examples.zh: 他隐居山中，过着壶中日月的悠闲生活。
examples.en: He lives secluded in the mountains in a leisurely little world of his own.

examples.zh: 醉里自成壶中日月，不问人间事。
examples.en: In his cups he makes a world of his own, indifferent to human affairs.

story.en: Fei Changfang saw an old man selling medicine who leapt into a pot each night; following him, he found a splendid palace inside the pot.
story.zh: 《后汉书·方术传》载费长房见卖药老翁悬壶于肆，及市罢，跳入壶中，随之入壶，见玉堂严丽。

usage.en: A Daoist-flavoured image for retirement and detachment; also written 壶中天地.
usage.zh: 带道家色彩，喻隐居自适；也作“壶中天地”。
